zones.label: Targeting & Exploiting a Wireless Network — Cradle to Grave (conceptual complexity view)

nodes.label: Objective defined
nodes.notes: Attacker motivation & value of the target set the whole effort budget.

nodes.label: Identify target org & sites
nodes.notes: Which physical locations even have the target network? Multiple sites multiply cost.

nodes.label: Remote wireless recon
nodes.notes: Public SSID databases, leaked floor plans, job ads naming kit. Passive, low risk — but incomplete.

nodes.label: Target identifiable remotely?
nodes.notes: Hidden SSID, common vendor names, many tenants in one building → ambiguity.

nodes.label: Assess feasibility & risk
nodes.notes: Legal exposure, guards, cameras, cost vs a cheaper vector (phishing, supply chain).

nodes.label: Choose another vector
nodes.notes: Most rational attackers stop here — wireless is often the hard path.

nodes.label: Within RF range?
nodes.notes: Walls, distance, interference. Directional antenna extends reach but needs line-of-sight & dwell time.

nodes.label: Get physically closer
nodes.notes: Car park, lobby, adjacent unit, drone. Each option adds exposure and time on target.

nodes.label: Access to standoff position?
nodes.notes: Fencing, access control, private land, patrols, hostile parking.

nodes.label: Establish observation post
nodes.notes: Stay long enough to capture signal without being noticed — the biggest real-world constraint.

nodes.label: Abort / burned
nodes.notes: Physical detection ends the operation and may attribute the actor.

nodes.label: Survey RF environment
nodes.notes: Which networks, bands, client counts. Enterprise vs consumer changes everything.

nodes.label: Which security model?
nodes.notes: Open / legacy / modern personal / enterprise 802.1X — each is a different difficulty class.

nodes.label: Enterprise 802.1X path
nodes.notes: Certificate / RADIUS-backed auth: far harder, often needs valid credentials or a device.

nodes.label: Capture opportunity?
nodes.notes: Needs the right clients present and active. Idle network = nothing to work with.

nodes.label: Attempt access
nodes.notes: Success depends on key strength, protections (PMF/lockouts), monitoring, and luck.

nodes.label: Iterate or wait
nodes.notes: Retry windows, come back another day, or fall back to a different network — time cost compounds.

nodes.label: Join network
nodes.notes: You're on the RF layer — but that's rarely the actual goal.

nodes.label: Segmented guest-only?
nodes.notes: Well-run networks isolate wireless from crown jewels — you may have reached a dead end.

nodes.label: Enumerate reachable assets
nodes.notes: NAC, internal firewalls and monitoring all fight you here.

nodes.label: Pivot toward target
nodes.notes: Every hop is another chance to trip detection / logging / EDR.

nodes.label: Achieve objective
nodes.notes: Access data / persistence / disruption — the reason for the whole chain.

nodes.label: Objective met
nodes.notes: The rare end state — reached only if every prior gate went the attacker's way.

nodes.label: Effort exceeds value → withdraw
nodes.notes: The most common outcome across all failed branches: cost outruns payoff.
